 Flyers vs. Blue Jackets: How to watch, lineups, and gamethread
 The Flyers are hosting the Blue Jackets in a battle between the two worst teams in the Metropolitan Division. Feel the excitement!
 Posted on October 27, 2026 October 27, 2026 by Thomas Williams 
 Image Credit: Heather Barry 
 The Philadelphia Flyers have another chance to get back in the win column and it’s up against the only other team we can truly call awful in the Metropolitan Division: The Columbus Blue Jackets. Will this be some garish hockey that leads to a 2-1 overtime win? Or will the lack of solid hockey so far for either team lead to some sort of 9-7 win where Michkov scores five points?
 Puck drop:  7:00 p.m.
 How to watch/listen: 
📺: NBCSP
📻: 97.5 The Fanatic
 Pregame reading
 Good news! Cam York has returned from his injury and is back in the Flyers lineup. But, the hockey gods sacrificed Rasmus Ristolainen to do it and he’s back on the IR. The Flyers will never have a healthy lineup. [BSH] 
 Should the Flyers take a run at Ivan Miroschnichenko? The Capitals are selling and taking whatever they can get for the 22-year-old winger since they don’t want to put him on waivers. [BSH] 
 Keith Jones has been all over North America lately, making trips to Chicago, Calgary, and New York to scout some hockey games. What is he looking for? Could this give us a clue to who the Flyers’ trade targets are? [BSH] 
 The Flyers’ 2023 NHL Draft class is looking GOOD. We’ll see four of them on the ice tonight, and there’s one other draftee over in Russia playing very well. [BSH]

 Storylines to watch
 Cam York is back! 
 He’s here! While his start to the season was extremely rough, there is still hope. Cam York was reportedly playing through an injury for a while and if we apply that knowledge to how he looked on the ice, it makes a whole lot more sense. He seemed slower, less active, more hesitant to make plays — all the stuff that leads to a defenseman looking absolutely awful.
 Now, he’s back and while the Flyers didn’t hold a formal morning skate, Rick Tocchet seemed to hint that he will be back beside Jamie Drysdale in his first game back. It does make sense. Nick Seeler probably should stop getting top-four minutes and now he’s settled in his role, alongside Hunter McDonald for some rough-and-tumble fun.
 What are the expectations for York? To not have a really bad giveaway that leads to a goal.
 No Emil Andrae revenge game? 
 It seems like our old friend Emil Andrae is stuck in the same spot as he was in Philadelphia. His first season outside of the Flyers organization and he’s still stuck as an extra defenseman, up in the press box, so the coach can play a large man who doesn’t do anything to make a team win hockey games, instead. You feel for the guy. We’ve largely loved his time with the Flyers and wish that he could really just be handed a top-four opportunity somewhere and have a coach with the most patience in the NHL, so that he can truly sink or swim in a bigger role. Now, he’s just stuck as someone who plays well but is considered not fast enough as a guy who is his size, despite doing things that lead to winning hockey games more often than not.
 Power play continues its hot streak? 
 The Flyers power play is good again, somehow. We have now reached a streak where we are starting to not get too worried about the man advantage and just assume it’s going to be two minutes of no goals happening. They have now gone four consecutive games with a power-play goal and have scored five in that span. It feels insane.
 Tonight, they might pot another one. The Blue Jackets have not been good on the penalty kill. They rank 27 in penalty kill percentage, and the underlyings don’t look too hot either. According to Evolving-Hockey, they have the ninth-highest shot attempts against rate and unblocked shot attempts against rate, while also averaging the fourth-highest expected goals against on the penalty kill. It’s an opportunity for the weapons that the Flyers do have, to get on the score sheet. It’s a weakness that hopefully they can exploit and get what is the difference between a mediocre loss and a great win.
